document_html: The financing company wishing to purchase the debt must provide the customer with the reference number of the payment transaction to facilitate the completion of procedures with the financing company selling the debt.

title: Article Ten
doc_path: Instructions for the Purchase of Consumer Finance Debts for Individuals Between Finance Companies
Chapter Two: Obligations of the Financing Company Wishing to Purchase the Debt
document_html: The financing company wishing to purchase the debt may not charge the customer any costs or fees for transferring the debt, except for early repayment fees or administrative fees.

title: Article Eleven
doc_path: Instructions for the Purchase of Consumer Finance Debts for Individuals Between Finance Companies
Chapter Two: Obligations of the Financing Company Wishing to Purchase the Debt
document_html: The financing company wishing to purchase the debt may not allow the customer to use the remaining amount of the financing—after the debt has been purchased—until it has received a release letter from the financing company selling the debt and obtained sufficient guarantees for granting the financing, along with any other regulatory and operational requirements, as applicable. These details must be clarified to the customer before proceeding with the debt purchase, as required by Article (7) of these instructions.

title: Article Twelve
doc_path: Instructions for the Purchase of Consumer Finance Debts for Individuals Between Finance Companies
Chapter Three: Obligations of the Financing Company Selling the Debt
document_html: The financing company selling the debt may not refuse to issue a statement of outstanding obligations or a letter confirming the debt upon the customer’s request. These statements and the letter must be issued within one business day from the date of receiving the request.

title: Article Thirteen
doc_path: Instructions for the Purchase of Consumer Finance Debts for Individuals Between Finance Companies
Chapter Three: Obligations of the Financing Company Selling the Debt
document_html: The financing company selling the debt must facilitate the debt transfer process and complete it within one business day from the date the requirements are fulfilled. The company may only refuse to approve any debt purchase request if there are sufficient justifications, which must be clearly explained to the customer in writing.

title: Article Fourteen
doc_path: Instructions for the Purchase of Consumer Finance Debts for Individuals Between Finance Companies
Chapter Three: Obligations of the Financing Company Selling the Debt
document_html: The financing company selling the debt must notify the customer of the debt repayment within one business day from the date of receiving the payment for the existing financing. The notification must include all required details, including the IBAN account number and the name of the bank or financial institution to which the debt amount is to be transferred.

title: Article Fifteen
doc_path: Instructions for the Purchase of Consumer Finance Debts for Individuals Between Finance Companies
Chapter Three: Obligations of the Financing Company Selling the Debt
document_html: The financing company selling the debt must issue a release letter to the customer within one business day from the date of receiving the payment for the existing financing and record this in the customer's credit record with credit information companies. An exception is made for customers with credit cards and/or monthly installment cards, for whom the release letter must be issued within seven business days.

title: Article Sixteen
doc_path: Instructions for the Purchase of Consumer Finance Debts for Individuals Between Finance Companies
Chapter Three: Obligations of the Financing Company Selling the Debt
document_html: The financing company selling the debt may not require the customer to pay any amounts for approving the sale of the debt, except in cases where there are delinquencies that the customer has not yet settled.

title: Article Seventeen
doc_path: Instructions for the Purchase of Consumer Finance Debts for Individuals Between Finance Companies
Chapter Three: Obligations of the Financing Company Selling the Debt
document_html: The financing company selling the debt may include early repayment amounts as specified in Article (84) of the implementing regulations of the Finance Companies Control Law in the debt confirmation letter.

title: Rules of Issuance and Operation of Credit Cards
doc_path: Rules of Issuance and Operation of Credit Cards
document_html:
• Rules of Issuance and Operation of Credit Cards

    Translated Document

    These Rules have been issued by circular No.(106911157), dated 23/12/1446H, corresponding to 19/06/2025G.

    • Chapter One General Provisions

      • Article 1

        The following terms and phrases, wherever used in these Rules, shall have the meanings indicated, unless the context requires otherwise: 

        TermDefinition
        SAMASaudi Central Bank
        Card IssuerAny entity supervised and regulated by SAMA and authorized to issue and finance credit cards. 
         
        CustomerThe natural or legal person who applies for or obtains the Credit Card from the card issuer.   
         
        Credit CardA card issued by the card issuer through which the customer can obtain goods, services or cash according to the credit limit, with the obligation to pay the amount due, thereafter or in accordance with the agreed payment arrangements. The definition includes monthly charge cards that require the customer to pay the full amount due on the due date. 
         
        Credit LimitThe maximum amount set by the card issuer that a customer can borrow using the credit card to obtain goods, services or cash. 
         
        Amount DueThe total amount used via credit card plus any fees or charges that the customer must pay in accordance with the payment arrangements agreed upon with the card issuer.  
        Minimum AmountThe minimum amount of the amount due that the customer must pay on or before the due date. 
         
        Due DateThe final date of the payment grace period by which the customer must pay the amount due according to the agreed payment arrangements. 
         
        Annual Percentage Rate "APR"The total cost of the credit card calculated according to the provisions of the rules governing calculation Annual Percentage Rate (APR) issued by SAMA. 
         
        Grace PeriodThe period during which the amount due can be paid without incurring any fees or costs, in accordance with the agreed payment arrangements.  
         
        Term CostThe cost charged on the amount due that has not been paid within the grace period, imposed on the cardholder as stipulated in the credit card agreement.  
         
        Late Payment FeesAn amount collected from the customer following the expiration of the grace period, resulting from non-payment of the amount due in accordance with the agreed payment arrangements. 
         
        Initial DisclosureBasic and clear information about the credit card, such as fees and charges, credit limit, and repayment terms, provided to the customer before entering into a credit card agreement.  
         
        Account StatementA periodic document issued by the card issuer and addressed to the customer, containing the data of the transactions made through the credit card during a certain period of time in accordance with Article (23) of these rules.
         
        Cash WithdrawalUtilize the credit limit by withdrawing from an ATM, making a transfer to a current account, or charging the e-wallet. 
         
        Credit RecordA report issued by credit information companies that contains a customer's credit information. 
         
        Authenticated ChannelsA recorded and verifiable means of communication that can be retrieved in written or electronic format. 
         
        Due Diligence Measures
                 		The process of recognizing and verifying the information of the real customer or beneficiary, which enables the card issuer to assess its risk exposure. 
         
        Unauthorized UseTransactions made using a credit card without the customer's consent or authorization. 
         
        Core FeatureBenefits and services that form part of the core services of the credit card, which are automatically provided without the need for a request or the payment of additional fees. 
         
        Optional FeatureBenefits and services that do not form part of the core benefits or services of the credit card, and are provided upon the customer’s request.
         
        DayA calendar day including weekends and holidays.
         
        Business DayA calendar day excluding weekends and holidays.
         

      • Article 2

        1. These rules aim to establish minimum requirements that a Card issuer must adhere to when issuing and operating a credit cards to promote disclosure, transparency and fair practices, as well as to limit credit risk.
           
        2. These rules shall apply to the Card Issuers. 
           

    • Chapter Two Credit Card Issuance

      • Article 3

        The card issuer is prohibited from issuing a credit card without receiving an explicit request from the customer through any of the authenticated channels, taking due diligence measures towards him, inquiring about his credit record, and assessing his creditworthiness by following a scientific method, and clear and written criteria and procedures in accordance with the relevant regulatory provisions and best practices in this field.

      • Article 4

        The card issuer must notify the customer via SMS upon acceptance or rejection of their credit card application within (3) business days from the date of the decision. In the event of rejection, the notification must include the reasons for the rejection and the procedure for submitting an objection.

      • Article 5

        1. When reissuing a credit card for any reason, the card issuer must notify the customer of the issuance of the card via SMS.
           
        2. The card issuer must enable the customer to accept or reject the reissued credit card, and the customer shall be deemed to have agreed to its issuance if he does not raise his objection within (14) days from the date of notification, or upon activation of the card.
           
        3. The reissued credit card must have the same category, terms, conditions, fees and charges as the original card, except if the card was issued based on the customer's request to upgrade the card to a higher category or downgrade the card to a lower category.  
           

      • Article 6

        1. The card issuer may, upon receiving a request from the customer through any of the authenticated channels, issue a supplementary credit card under the customer’s account, either in the customer’s name or in the name of another party referred to as (the supplementary credit cardholder), the card issuer must notify the customer of their responsibility for all obligations arising from the use of this card.  
           
        2. The card issuer shall conduct due diligence measures on the supplementary credit cardholder and notify the customer through any of the authenticated channels about the transactions made through the supplementary credit card. The customer may request that the supplementary credit cardholder also be notified about the transactions made through the card. 
           

      • Article 7

        The card issuer is prohibited from issuing a credit card to customers under the age of (18) Hijri years, except where the card is a supplementary card issued in accordance with the requirements for issuing supplementary credit cards as set out in these Rules.

      • Article 8

        1. The card issuer shall not allow the use of the credit card until it has been activated by the customer through any of the authenticated channels.
           
        2. The card issuer may not charge the annual fee for the credit card until the customer activates the card. The card issuer may cancel the card if it is not activated within (90) days from the date of issuance without charging a fee, and with notifying the customer via SMS of the cancellation. 
           

      • Article 9

        The card issuer shall periodically update the information obtained when conducting due diligence measures on the customer and the supplementary cardholder, in accordance with the level and degree of risk of each of them, enabling the updating of that information through any of the authenticated channels, with verification of its authenticity through a reliable and independent source. 

      • Article 10

        The card issuer must register the credit card information - after the customer's consent - in the credit record, including the credit limit and the amount due, and update this information in accordance with the relevant regulatory provisions. 
         

    • Chapter Three Credit Card Agreement

      • Article 11

        The card issuer shall provide the customer through any of the authenticated channels with an initial disclosure that includes the contents set out in Article (13) of these rules, and obtain the customer’s acknowledgment of reading and understanding the disclosure. 

      • Article 12

        The card issuer must obtain the customer's signature on the credit card agreement in a written form, whether electronic or paper-based, in accordance with the relevant regulatory provisions.  
         

      • Article 13

        The Credit Card Agreement must be in Arabic (or in English if requested by the customer), and must include all the terms and conditions of using the card, including the following:

        1. Fees and charges associated with the use of a credit card in the form provided in Appendix A of these rules.
           
        2. Account statement issuance date.
           
        3. Due date.
           
        4. Credit limit.
           
        5. Minimum amount.
           
        6. Payment terms including grace period.
           
        7. Default provisions.
           
        8. Credit card risks and how to avoid them.
           
        9. The core and optional features, the mechanism for utilizing them, and their associated costs must be clearly outlined, in accordance with Appendix (B) of these Rules.
           
        10. The customer's right to cancel the card within (90) days from the date of receiving the card without activation.
           
        11. Consequences of paying only the minimum amount.
           
        12. The due date of the annual fees, if any.
           
        13. The customer is responsible for all obligations arising from the use of the supplementary credit card if issued. 
           

      • Article 14

        The card issuer must notify the customer via SMS at least (14) days prior to the due date of the annual fees, if any, and enable the customer to cancel the card within this period without charging the fees.

      • Article 15

        1. The card issuer must notify the customer - through any of the authenticated channels- at least 30 days prior to any change in the terms and conditions of use of the credit card, provided that SMS messages are among the authenticated channels for this notification, and the notice must include, at a minimum, the following:

           1.1Clearly and conspicuously state changes to fees, costs and benefits. 
           
           1.2Direct communication with the card issuer to find out about changes to the terms and conditions. 
           
           1.3The customer's right to terminate the credit card agreement within (14) days from the date of notification, indicating the specific mechanism for this, provided that it is easy and convenient. 
           
           1.4Stipulating the refund of the annual fee for the credit card after deducting the charges for the period used if the customer wishes to terminate the agreement. 
           
             
        2. The card issuer is prohibited from amending the terms and conditions related to the promotional benefits included in the credit card agreement prior to the expiration of the specified promotional period. The card issuer is also prohibited from making any increase to the fees and charges associated with the credit card, except for fees and charges imposed by third parties, provided that the customer is notified at least (30) days prior to the effective date of such change.
           
        3. The card issuer shall enable the customer to terminate the credit card agreement within (14) days from the date of notification of the change in the terms and conditions of use of the credit card , The annual fee of the credit card shall be refunded after deducting the fees for the period used, and appropriate solutions shall be offered for the payment of the amount due.

         

    • Chapter Four Reimbursement

      • Article 16

        1. The card issuer shall set the due date on the same date of each month, and treat payments made by midnight on the due date as paid without delay.
           
        2. The card issuer shall take into account cases where the customer may face payment difficulties due to a technical failure or a system update, and shall treat the amounts paid after resolving the issue as if they were paid on time.
           

      • Article 17

        1. The card issuer is prohibited from charging late payment fees without granting the customer a grace period of at least (25) days from the account statement issuance date.
           
        2. The card issuer is prohibited from reducing the monthly minimum amount to less than 5% of the amount due. 
           
        3. The card issuer is prohibited from forcing the customer to pay only the minimum amount. The card issuer must also make all payment options available to the customer, including the option to pay the full amount due.
           
        4. The card issuer is prohibited from changing the agreed-upon payment method without a documented request from the customer. An exception to this is allowing the customer to pay the minimum amount (5% of the amount due) in cases where the full amount due is not available.
           

      • Article 18

        The card issuer must clearly explain the consequences of paying only the minimum amount when payment is made available, in addition to including this information in the credit card agreement and the account statement.

      • Article 19

        As an exception to the provisions of the Debt Collection Regulations and Procedures, the customer is considered defaulted if he does not pay the minimum amount for more than (90) consecutive days. In this case, the card issuer may suspend the use of the credit card and communicate with the customer to collect the amount due, provided that appropriate solutions are offered to settle the amount before proceeding with legal actions.

      • Article 20

        Card Issuers are prohibited from increasing the term cost on the amount due as a result of delinquency or default.

      • Article 21

        The card issuer shall enable the customer to cancel the credit card - at any time - without requiring his presence at the issuer's premises, after paying the amount due and submitting a request for cancellation through any of the authenticated channels. In this case, the card issuer must issue a clearance letter and update the credit record within (7) business days from the date of canceling the card.

    • Chapter Five Account Statement

      • Article 22

        The card issuer shall provide the customer monthly -through any of the authenticated channels- with the account statement (25) days before the due date. The account statement shall be in Arabic (or in English if requested by the customer). The customer shall be notified upon its issuance via SMS, including the amount due, the minimum amount, and the due date.

      • Article 23

        1. The account statement must include the following data and information 

          1.1The time period covered by the account statement.  
           
          1.2Opening balance (credit card account balance at the beginning of the account statement period). 
           
          1.3Closing balance (the credit card account balance after the last transaction in the account statement period). 
           
          1.4Details of financial transactions (type of transaction, date, amount, merchant data), taking into account that the data for international financial transactions should include the original amount of the transaction in foreign currency, the exchange rate used to convert to local currency, the corresponding amount in local currency after conversion, and any fees charged for the transaction.
           
          1.5Total transaction amounts. 
           
          1.6Payments and refunds (any payments charged or refunds to the account, including the amount and date of the payment or refund). 
           
          1.7Total payment amounts
           
          1.8Details of fees and costs. 
           
          1.9The total amount of fees and charges. 
           
          1.10The amount due, indicating the amount subject to the term cost and how it is calculated. 
           
          1.11Due date. 
           
          1.12Annual Percentage Rate (APR) 
           
          1.13The mechanism for objecting to the account statement, including the deadline for doing so. 
           
          1.14An illustrative example in red text shall include the following information:
           
           1.The period required for the customer to repay an amount of SAR 7,000 or the actual statement balance by paying only the minimum amount.
           
           2.The total amount, including cost, that the customer will pay by the end of the period as a result of choosing to pay the minimum amount.
           
        2. The card issuer must observe the definition of terms in the account statement.
           

      • Article 24

        The card issuer shall enable the customer to object to the account statement within a period of not less than (30) days from the date of notification of its issuance, in accordance with the following controls:

        1. authenticated channels for receiving objections are defined.  
           
        2. Develop a form for submitting an objection that includes the customer's name, the data objected to, and the reasons for the objection.
           
        3. Contact the customer to complete any information or documents to verify the validity of the objection within no more than seven (7) days from the date of submission.
           
        4. The customer shall be provided, through any of the authenticated channels, with a reference number to track the objection, along with the expected time frame for resolution, which shall not exceed 90 days from the date the objection is deemed complete. The card issuer may extend this period to 120 days from the date of objection completion if necessary, provided that the customer is notified.
           
        5. Provide the customer through any of the authenticated channels with the result of the objection study, indicating the mechanism for objecting to the result and escalation.
           
        6. The customer shall not be required to pay any amounts related to the objection until the objection has been fully resolved.
           

      • Article 25

        If the customer's objection is found to be valid, the card issuer shall immediately correct the error, including returning any amounts deducted in error and correcting the information recorded in the credit record, taking into account the customer's notification through any of the authenticated channels.

      • Article 26

        If the customer's objection is invalid, the card issuer shall explain the reasons for the invalidity of the objection along with any necessary proof.

    • Chapter Six Credit Card Transactions

      • Article 27

        The card issuer must use the Saudi Riyal as the basis for calculating and disclosing credit card transactions, except for cards issued in currencies other than the Saudi Riyal.

      • Article 28

        Without prejudice to the provisions of the relevant regulations: the card issuer may allow cash withdrawals provided that it does not exceed 30% of the card's credit limit.

      • Article 29

        The card issuer shall enable the customer for additional amounts to be credited to the credit limit in accordance with the following rules:

        1. The additional amount shall be used to settle post-deposit transactions without charging a term cost or fees-except for fees incurred by the card issuer on behalf of third party-and provided such fees do not exceed limits specified in Article (48) of these rules. 
           
        2. The customer shall be allowed to redeem the additional amount at any time, with no charge for the redemption process.
           
        3. The additional amount is clearly shown on the credit card statement.
           
        4. The terms and conditions of the additional amount within the credit card agreement. 
           

      • Article 30

        The card issuer must include in the agreements concluded with its merchant customers the right not to impose additional fees on the amount of the product or service in the event of payment using a credit card, whether through POS machines or e-commerce websites and electronic applications, as well as the right not to photograph, copy or record the information contained in the credit card.

      • Article 31

        1. The card issuer shall notify the customer via SMS immediately about the financial transactions that are carried out using the credit card.
           
        2. The credit card notification shall include -as a minimum- the following: the merchant's name -if available-, and the transaction date, and the transaction amount, and the transaction fees, and the total amount due, and the remaining balance of the credit limit, the exchange rate, and the international purchase transaction fees for international transactions. 
           

      • Article 32

        The card issuer is prohibited from increasing the credit limit of a credit card without receiving an explicit request from the customer through any of the authenticated channels and re-evaluating the creditworthiness.

      • Article 33

        The card issuer is prohibited from allowing the credit limit of a credit card to be exceeded.

      • Article 34

        The card issuer must periodically educate customers- through all available channels- about the proper use of the credit card, and the mechanism for dealing with the loss, theft, or unauthorized use of the card.

      • Article 35

        If the card issuer needs to reduce the credit limit of the credit card for any reason, the issuer must notify the customer in advance through any of the authenticated channels with an explanation of the justification.

      • Article 36

        The card issuer is prohibited from collecting any credit card payments without prior authorization or documented consent from the customer.

      • Article 37

        The card issuer must deposit the amounts transferred between the customer's current account and the credit card account at the same bank on the date of the transfer, and the issuer is not entitled to charge a transfer fees for this transaction.

      • Article 38

        1. Before activating any optional credit card feature, the card issuer must receive an explicit request from the customer through any of the authenticated channels, and obtain their consent to incur the fees.
        2. The card issuer must enable the customer to view the details of the basic and optional benefits through the application or the card issuer's website.
           

      • Article 39

        1. The card issuer must notify the customer -via SMS- at least 14 days before the expiration of any benefits associated with the credit card.
        2. The card issuer must notify the customer-via SMS- regarding any available reward points (if applicable), at least thirty (30) days prior to their expiration date, and must send a reminder notification again seven (7) days before the expiration date.

      • Article 40

        The card issuer must, if a rewards program is available, provide an estimation calculator on its website and electronic application, through which the customer can calculate the rewards they are entitled to (earned and redeemed) based on financial transactions carried out using the credit card, in accordance with the rewards program policy approved by the issuer.

    • Chapter Seven Reporting Unauthorized Use

      • Article 41

        The card issuer must provide a 24-hour toll-free number and other authenticated channels to receive customer reports from inside or outside the Kingdom regarding lost or stolen credit cards or unauthorized use.

      • Article 42

        The card issuer must suspend the credit card immediately upon receiving the customer's report of loss, theft, or unauthorized use of the card, and notify the customer via SMS, providing them with a reference number to follow up on the status of the report.

      • Article 43

        1. The card issuer shall suspend the transaction amount resulting from the unauthorized use as soon as it receives the customer or supplementary credit cardholder's report of the unauthorized use. 
           
        2. The card issuer may request the necessary clarifications and documents to verify the validity of the report of unauthorized use. 
           
        3. The processing of a report of unauthorized use shall not exceed seven (7) business days from the date of receipt of the report, including reversing the transaction amount and crediting the credit card account, and considering reactivation or reissuance of the card after taking appropriate precautionary measures.
           

      • Article 44

        The card issuer is responsible for credit card operations after receiving a customer or supplementary credit cardholder's report of credit card loss, theft, or unauthorized use.

    • Chapter Eight Fees and Charges Associated with the Credit Card

      • Article 45

        The card issuer must include in the initial disclosure and the credit card agreement a detailed table of all fees and charges associated with the credit card in the format provided in Appendix(A) of these rules.

      • Article 46

        The card issuer must provide an estimated calculator within the website and online application through which the customer can calculate the approximate cost of an international transaction using a credit card, taking into account all the parameters that will use to calculate the cost, such as the exchange rate, international purchase transaction fees, and stating that this cost is approximate and may vary based on changes in exchange rates.

      • Article 47

        The card issuer shall include in the initial disclosure, the credit card agreement, and the account statement an illustrative example of the calculation of the term cost, and the card issuer may be guided by the formula provided in Annex (c) of these rules.

      • Article 48

        The card issuer is prohibited from exceeding the maximum credit card transactions and processing fees shown in the table below for individual customers.

        Transaction/ProcedureMaximum Fee (Excluding Value-Added Tax)

        1.   Cash withdrawal (ATM Withdrawal) 

         

        2.    Cash withdrawal (Transfer to Current Account)

        		Not to exceed 3% of the transaction amount, with a maximum limit of (75) SAR.
        3.  Cash withdrawal (E-Wallet recharge)Free.
         
        4.   Wrong dispute on the transactions and the account statement25 SAR.
         
        5.   Credit card inquiry via ATM1.5 SAR.
         
        6.   Use your credit card locally at POS terminals or Online PurchasesFree.
         
        7.   Reissuance of Credit Card (Lost, Damaged, Incorrect PIN)15 SAR.
         
        8.   Late Payment50 SAR.
         
        9.   International purchase Transaction Fees2 % of the transaction amount
         

    • Chapter 9 Final Provisions

      • Article 49

        1. The provisions of these rules are without prejudice to the provisions contained in the relevant instructions issued by SAMA, including, but not limited to, the following:

          1.1Final Consumer Protection Principles and Rules
           
          1.2Responsible Lending Principles for Individuals Customers
           
          1.3Debt Collection Regulations and Procedures for Individual Customers
           
          1.4Rules for Advertising Products and Services Provided by Financial Institutions. 
           
          1.5Rules Governing Calculation of Annual Percentage Rate (APR) . 
           
          1.6Disclosure of Interest Rates on Financing and Savings Products. 
           
          1.7Principles of Conduct and Work Ethics in Financial Institutions .
           
          1.8Regulations for Consumer Financing . 
           
          1.9Counter-Fraud Framework. 
           
          1.10Cyber Security Framework. 
           
          1.11Business Continuity Management Framework . 
           
          1.12Instructions for Services Provided to Persons with Disabilities in Financial Institutions . 
           
        2. In the event of a conflict between the provisions of these rules and the provisions of the rules issued by international payment companies, the provisions of these rules shall prevail.
           

      • Article 50

        These rules shall be implemented within (90) days from the date of their publication on SAMA's website, and shall replace the Regulations of Issuance and Operating Credit and Monthly Charge Cards, communicated by SAMA Circular No. (361000090389) dated 26/06/1436H.

    • Appendix A: Credit Card Fees and Charges Disclosure Form

      MThe name of the drawingThe amount of the fee
      1Annual Percentage Rate (APR): 
      The discount rate at which the present value of all installments and other payments due from the beneficiary—representing the total amount payable by the beneficiary—is equal to the present value of the financing amount disbursements available to the beneficiary, on the date the financing amount or the first disbursement thereof becomes available to the beneficiary, in accordance with the provisions of the Rules Governing Calculation of Annual Percentage Rate (APR) issued by SAMA.
             		 
      2Term cost:
      The value of the term on the outstanding amount due and unpaid during the grace period. 
             		 
      3Annual Fee:
      An amount charged annually for the activation or use of the card.
             		 
      4Cash withdrawal fees (ATM cash withdrawal and transfer to the current account):
      An amount charged for a transfer from the available credit card balance to the customer's checking account.
             		 
      5Cash withdrawal fees (E-wallet recharge):
      An amount charged for recharging the customer's e-wallet from the available credit card balance.
             		 
      6Fees for wrong dispute on transactions and account statement: 
      An amount charged when a dispute is filed regarding a transaction or the account statement that, after review and investigation, is found to be correct.
             		 
      7

      International Purchase Transaction Fee: 

      An amount charged for using a credit card to purchase goods or services whose currency is different from the card's currency or outside Saudi Arabia. 
      Illustrative example:
       

      Transaction amountExchange rateAmount in rialsInternational purchase transaction FeeAmount due
           
      		 
      8Late payment fees: 
      An amount collected from the customer after the grace period has ended without payment of the amount due, in accordance with the agreed payment arrangements. 
             		 

      *The card issuer must include any other fees and charges associated with the credit card, clearly defined in a manner that is easy for the customer to understand.

      *The card issuer must highlight the Annual Percentage Rate (APR) and the Term Cost using a different font and color from the rest of the information.

    • Appendix B: Disclosure Form for Basic and Optional Benefits

      M

      Details

       

       

       

      1

      Features Based on Promotional Offers – if any:

      Details of any temporary or permanent promotional offer provided to the customer must be clearly disclosed, including the features, discounts, or waivers of specific fees, along with the duration of the offer and all applicable terms and conditions, in a clear manner that is easy for the customer to understand.

      Illustrative Example:

      *The promotional offer is non-modifiable, and the customer shall be notified at least fourteen (14) days prior to its expiration.

       

       

       

      2

      Rewards Programs and Similar Offerings – if any:

      The program’s details must be clearly disclosed, including its mechanism, methods of redemption, validity period, and all applicable terms and conditions, in a manner that is easy for the customer to understand.

      Validity Period

      Example: Cashback ProgramExample: Based on merchant category, cashback percentage, and a maximum cashback limitExample: Direct cashback or credited on statementExample: 24 months from the date of issuance

      *The customer will be notified via SMS at least fourteen (14) days prior to the expiration of the benefit eligibility period under the program.

      *The customer will be notified via SMS at least thirty (30) days prior to any modification to the program. The customer shall have the right to terminate the agreement within fourteen (14) days from the date of notification and to receive a refund of the annual fee, after deducting the fee for the period used.

      3

      Other basic and optional features - if any:

      The details of any additional features, along with all applicable terms and conditions, must be clearly disclosed in a manner that is easy for the customer to understand.

      *This Appendix constitutes the minimum level of disclosure regarding basic and optional features, and the card issuer must give due importance to ensuring the customer’s understanding of these features.
