Disclosure of Accounts of Bankrupt and Insolvent: 
 
182.In case any person contacts a DTFC to inquire about or disclose transactions, accounts balances or banking relationships related to his debtors or his clients because of bankruptcy or insolvency, the DTFC should direct him to submit a request of that to the competent judicial authority.

title: General Rules for the Operation of Accounts
doc_path: 3 Part III: Account Opening and Operating Rules and Regulations
General Rules for the Operation of Accounts
document_html:
183.The operation of the accounts shall be primarily the responsibility of the Account Holder and persons authorized by the Account Holder.
 
184.Account holders and its authorized person can operate the accounts either passing through written instructions duly signed and stamps or through digital mean.
 
185.DTFCs must facilitate its customer by availing standard forms and agreements to pass written instructions to operate accounts such as Forms use to initiate, cancel and/or roll over a Term Deposit Deal or deposit or withdraw funds from General Account etc.
 
186.DTFCs must verify the authenticity and validity of signatures provided on the form by comparing the specimen signatures in the signature form.
 
187.DTFCs must verify the identity of account holder and/or authorized person at the time receiving written instructions to operate General Account by obtaining a copy of his / her identity documents.
 
188.DTFCs should facilitate its customers to operate their accounts remotely i.e. through digital channels. In case DTFCs provides such facility, DTFCs must ensure the account holder or its authorized person goes through dual sign-in verification process before access to view and operate the accounts are provided.
 
189.In addition, DTFCs must provide maker / checker functionality to the account holder relating to juristic person on its digital channels before DTFCs receives the request to process. Maker / Checker means that two different individuals are required (one to initiate the request and other to approve). Both these individuals must go through dual sign-in verification process.
 
190.DTFCs must NOT accept physical cash to deposit funds to or disburse cash to withdraw fund from the General Account.
 
191.Persons authorized to operate bank accounts of juristic persons shall be authorized by authorized individuals, which are authorized by public or private approval, such as by the Board of Directors, Partners, Employer or any person designated by the Owner or by Officials of the establishment or entity.
 
192.The sole purpose of the General Account is to facilitate operations of Term Deposit Accounts therefore DTFCs should not allow usage of the account for any other purpose such as making payments to third parties i.e. a payment where beneficiary is not the DTFC where General Account is held or Account Holder itself.
 
193.DTFCs shall not allow General Account to be used receive funds from third parties.
 
194.Under no circumstances, DTFCs will overdraw any General Account or any Term Deposit Account.

title: General Account
doc_path: 3 Part III: Account Opening and Operating Rules and Regulations
document_html:
195.As stated in Section 1.1, the sole purpose of the General Account is to facilitate operations of Term Deposit Accounts.
 
Credit Entries Rules 
 
General rules 
 
196.General Account can ONLY be funded i.e. credited through the following operations:
 
 i.Funds received directly from accountholder's Bank Account(s).
 ii.Funds received from the account holders' Term Deposit Account
 
Funds received directly from accountholder's Bank accounts) 
 
197.DTFC must match the name of remitter with the name on General Account before crediting the funds to the General Account. In case of difference, DTFC must return the funds back to the remitter.
 
198.DTFCs must record the name of the remitter, IBAN number of the remitter and value date as part of posting the credit entry to the General Account.
 
199.DTFC may receive funds from multiple accountholder's bank accounts to fund a General Account. In this case, DTFC should proceed with credit the General Account provided conditions laid down in 9.2.3.1 and 9.2.3.2 are satisfied.
 
Funds received from the account holders' Term Deposit Account(s) 
 
200.Upon maturity of Term Deposit Account, DTFC must credit the principle and profit amount separately to the General Account from which Term Deposit Account was funded in the first place.
 
201.DTFCs must record the details of the credit i.e. whether it is Principle or Profit, account number of Term Deposit Account / Term Deposit deal number, profit rate, currency, deal date, start date, maturity date and amount part of posting the credit entry to the General Deposit Account. In case of Islamic Term Deposit Account, details of underlying commodity, quantity and price sold & bought of the commodity must be recorded.
 
202.Upon cancellation of the Term Deposit Account, DTFC must credit principle amount only to the General Account from which Term Deposit Account was funded in the first place.
 
203.DTFC can credit the General Account from multiple Term Deposit Accounts (upon cancellation or maturity), provided conditions laid down in 9.2.4.1, 9.2.4.2 and 9.2.4.3 are met.
 
Debit Entries Rules 
 
General Rules 
 
204.Funds from General Account can only be withdrawn i.e. debited through the following operations:
 
 i.Funds withdrawn by accountholder of the General Account.
 ii.Funds remitted to the Term Deposit Account
 iii.Deductible charges
 
205.Funds can only be withdrawn from General Account based on the instructions or agreement of the accountholder.
 
Funds withdrawn by accountholder of the General Account 
 
206.From time to time accountholder may wish to withdraw the funds from General Account. Finance must remit the funds back to the same Bank account of the account holder from which General Account was initially funded i.e. the source.
 
207.In case, General Account was initially funded from multiple accounts belong to the accountholder, DTFCs can remit the funds back to any of the accounts from which General Account was initially funded as per the instructions or agreement of the account holder.
 
Transfers between General Accounts 
 
208.If account holder have more than one General Accounts in a DTFC, then transfers between these accounts within the DTFC is permissible provided all General Accounts are held under the same name.

title: Term Deposit Account
doc_path: 3 Part III: Account Opening and Operating Rules and Regulations
document_html:
209.The minimum tenor for the deposits is six months.
 
210.As stated in section 1.2., the purpose of the Term Deposit Account is hold the funds for an agreed period accruing profit at an agreed rate as per Term Deposit Deal, therefore a Term Deposit Account only reflects term and status of one only Term Deal.
 
211.Term Deposit Account must hold and record all the information relating to the terms of the related Term Deposit Deal, which should include, at the minimum, identification of Currency, Deal Capture date, Deal Trade Date, Deal Start Date, Deal Maturity Date, Days convention (30/360, Actual/360, etc.), Principle amount, Profit rate, Total profit amount at maturity and total profit amount accrued up to date of the inquiry, status of the deal (active, cancelled, matured etc.).
 
212.In case of Sharia Compliant Term Deposit Deal, DTFCs must hold and record the related commodity information such as, at the minimum, the identification of commodity, quantity of the commodity, selling and buying prices, names and statuses (principal / agent) of parties/broker involved etc.
 
213.Upon start date of Term Deposit Deal, Finance must debit Principle amount from General Amount and credit the Principle amount to Term Deposit account.
 
214.Upon maturity or cancellation of the Term Deposit Account, DTFCs must return the funds held in Term Deposit Accounts back to the same linked General Deposit Account.
 
215.DTFCs must NOT facilitate Currency Conversion or Currency Translation to its Account Holders.

title: Term Deposit Deal
doc_path: 3 Part III: Account Opening and Operating Rules and Regulations
document_html:
216.DTFCs must ensure it has evidence that its Account Holders agreed to the terms of the Term Deposit Deal through a sign Term Deposit Deal Agreement.
 
217.DTFCs must send confirmation to its Account Holders stating all terms of the Term Deposit Deal and ensure its Account holder agrees to terms through signing and having account holders seal on the confirmation.

title: Chapter 16: Closing of the Account
doc_path: 3 Part III: Account Opening and Operating Rules and Regulations
document_html:
218.If the account holder wishes to terminate his dealings with the DTFCs, the account holder must submit a request to close his account.
 
219.The DTFCs must reject the client's request to close the account in case the account is frozen or blocked by SAMA or a Judicial Order.
 
220.In the event that the account is exposed to an unresolvable problem(s) of verification, the DTFC must lock the account and return the money / balance to the source.
 
221.In connection with a suspicion of customer transactions (money laundering, terrorist financing, etc.), the Financial must apply anti-money laundering and terrorist financing rules, including reporting.
 
222.In case of opening, the account and the customer deposited into it and then withdraw from it and the balance became zero and continued without balance or deal for 4 years; DTFCs must send the notification of closing to account holder.
 
223.DTFCs must save all documentation and notices relating to the closure of the account in the client’s file.
 
224.DTFCs shall add the items related to the closure of the account within the terms of the account opening agreement or in a paper attached to the agreement.

title: Chapter 17: Statement and Audit Confirmation
doc_path: 3 Part III: Account Opening and Operating Rules and Regulations
document_html:
225.DTFCs shall provide at least once in year the statements of accounts of all the accounts (General and Term Deposit Accounts) to its accountholders.
 
226.DTFCs shall also provide Audit Confirmation to accountholders Auditors based on the held add the items related to the closure of the account within the terms of the account opening agreement or in a paper attached to the agreement.

title: Chapter 18: Final Provisions
doc_path: 3 Part III: Account Opening and Operating Rules and Regulations
document_html: 227.These Rules thereto shall be effective as of the date of its issuance.

title: Article 1: Definitions
doc_path: Rules of Licensing Finance Support Activities
Chapter I: Definitions and General Provisions
document_html:
1.The terms and phrases used in these Rules shall have the same meaning as defined in the Finance Companies Control Law and its Implementing Regulation. 
 
2.For the purpose of applying the provisions of these Rules, the following terms and phrases -wherever mentioned herein- shall have the meanings assigned thereto, unless the context otherwise requires.
 
 2.1Finance Support Activities: activities that support or complement finance activities in order to achieve competition in accordance with the bank instructions. These activities include aggregation activity and any other activity approved by the bank. Finance debt collection activity is excluded.
 
 2.2Finance Support Company: a person licensed by the bank to perform one or more of the finance support activities in accordance with the Law and its Implementing Regulation, and these Rules.
 
 2.3Aggregation Activity: a service provided to link clients with finance companies according to their credit obligations and solvency to offer financial services through an electronic platform for a charge.

title: Article 2: Scope of Application
doc_path: Rules of Licensing Finance Support Activities
Chapter I: Definitions and General Provisions
document_html: These Rules shall apply to companies licensed by the bank to engage in finance support activity.

title: Article 3: Purpose
doc_path: Rules of Licensing Finance Support Activities
Chapter I: Definitions and General Provisions
document_html: The objective of these Rules is to establish licensing requirements and controls for finance support activities and to monitor these activities.

title: Article 4: General Provisions
doc_path: Rules of Licensing Finance Support Activities
Chapter I: Definitions and General Provisions
document_html: Without prejudice to the Finance Companies Control Law and its Implementing Regulation, the finance support activities license application shall be submitted to the bank in accordance with the requirements, controls and procedures set forth in these Rules and the instructions issued by the bank in this regard from time to time.

title: Article 5: License Application
doc_path: Rules of Licensing Finance Support Activities
document_html:
The applicant for a license to practice finance support activities shall submit the license application to the bank. The request shall specify the activities to be licensed, and shall be attached with the following:
 
1.a completed license application in the form provided by the bank;
 
2.Memorandum of incorporation and articles of association (if any) of the company;
 
3.a list of founding members or shareholders and partners and the shares they own in the company and the percentage thereof; an irrevocable bank guarantee, if the applicant is a company in the process of incorporation, with an amount equivalent to the minimum capital for the support activity(ies), issued in favor of the bank by a domestic bank and automatically renewed until the capital is paid in full. This guarantee shall be released upon the request of the founding members in the following cases:
 
 i.if the capital is paid in cash;
 
 ii.if the license application is withdrawn; or
 
 iii.if the license application is rejected by the bank.
 
4.draft agreements and proposed contracts with third parties; and
 
5.Any other documents, data, and information required by the bank.

title: Article 6: Paid-Up Capital
doc_path: Rules of Licensing Finance Support Activities
document_html:
1.Pursuant to the provisions of the Companies Law, the minimum capital for the finance support company shall be as follows:
 
 (a)(SAR 2,000,000) for aggregation activity.
 
 (b)The bank shall set the minimum capital for the finance support company that engages in other support activities approved by the bank.
 
2.The bank may stipulate higher or lower minimum capital based on the prevailing market conditions, or if it deems that the proposed business model or the nature of activities or the proposed geographical scope requires so, taking into consideration the risk profile of the activity.

title: Article 7: Management Requirements
doc_path: Rules of Licensing Finance Support Activities
document_html:
All candidates for supervisory and executive positions in a finance support company must:
 

(a)meet the professional legal competence requirements set by the bank;
 
(b)be permanent residents in Saudi Arabia;
 
(c)be professionally qualified, and have appropriate experience in the same field;
 
(d)not have violated any of the provisions or regulations of the Capital Market Law, the Banking Control Law, the Cooperative Insurance Companies Control Law or Finance Laws; and
 
(e)not have been previously convicted of an offense impinging upon integrity, unless rehabilitated in accordance with the laws or the Implementing Regulation of the Finance Companies Control Law.

title: Article 8: Initial Approval
doc_path: Rules of Licensing Finance Support Activities
document_html: Within thirty (30) working days from completion of requirements, the bank shall grant either an initial approval or a justified rejection. The bank will assess the competitiveness and soundness of the industry and the quality of services provided.

title: Article 9: Provision of Required Information
doc_path: Rules of Licensing Finance Support Activities
document_html:
1.The license applicant shall provide any additional information or documents required by the bank within (15) working days.
 
2.In case of failure to meet the period requirement specified in Paragraph (1) of this Article, the bank may reject the license application.

title: Article 10: Establishment
doc_path: Rules of Licensing Finance Support Activities
document_html: The founding members shall establish the finance support company within (6) months from the bank’s initial approval, and provide the bank with a copy of the company’s commercial register stating the licensed activities for initial approval. The initial approval will expire after (6) months, unless the bank agrees to extend the period.

title: Article 11: License
doc_path: Rules of Licensing Finance Support Activities
document_html:
1.The bank may take the necessary actions to ensure that the finance support company meets the bank’s requirements, such as making supervisory or inspection visits to the company headquarters, meeting its executives and reviewing its systems, procedures and records.
 
2.Upon verification of the applicant compliance with the requirements set forth herein, the bank shall issue the license for finance support activities.
 
3.The finance support company shall not engage in any activity not licensed by the bank.

title: Article 12: Scope of License
doc_path: Rules of Licensing Finance Support Activities
document_html: The license shall specify the activities that the finance support company is licensed to carry out, and the bank may restrict the license to special conditions.

title: Article 13: Validity of License
doc_path: Rules of Licensing Finance Support Activities
document_html: The license shall be valid for three (3) years and may be renewed by the bank upon the request of the company. The company shall submit a written renewal request to the bank at least (3) months prior to the expiration of the license.

title: Article 14: Amendment of License
doc_path: Rules of Licensing Finance Support Activities
document_html: The finance support company may request to amend the license, or to amend any condition or limitation in the license, provided that such request is based on reasonable justifications. Any documents, information or studies required by the bank shall be attached to the request.

title: Article 15: Revocation of License
doc_path: Rules of Licensing Finance Support Activities
document_html:
The bank may revoke the license in the following cases:

1.Upon the request of the finance support company, taking into account the rights of the creditors and beneficiaries as well as the soundness of the financial system.
 
2.If the finance support company has submitted false information or failed to disclose material information that should have been provided for licensing purposes.
 
3.If the finance support company has violated the requirements of these Rules, the provisions of finance laws, or the bank’s instructions.
 
4.If the finance support company has not carried out the licensed activities within (6) months from the date of issuance of license.
 
5.If the operations of the finance support company have been suspended for more than (3) consecutive months, or for (6) non-consecutive months without obtaining the bank’s prior written no-objection.

title: Article 16: License Expiry
doc_path: Rules of Licensing Finance Support Activities
document_html:
The license shall be legally expired in the following cases:

1.Non-renewal of expired license;
 
2.Appointment of liquidator for the finance support company; or
 
3.Commencement of bankruptcy proceedings under the Bankruptcy Law.

title: Article 17: Effects of License Revocation or Expiry
doc_path: Rules of Licensing Finance Support Activities
Article 17: Effects of License Revocation or Expiry
document_html: Revocation or expiry of license shall result in liquidation of the finance support company. Such company shall be notified in writing of license revocation, and shall be given a period of (6) months to conduct liquidation. The bank may also appoint a liquidator.

title: Article 18: Internal Policies and Procedures
doc_path: Rules of Licensing Finance Support Activities
document_html:
The finance support company shall:
 
1.develop internal policies and procedures to ensure compliance with these Rules, the bank’s instructions, and relevant laws; and
 
2.develop written organizational policies which cover internal organization, governance, risk management, compliance, outsourcing and human resources. These policies shall be approved by the highest authority in the company.

title: Article 19: Requirements for Information Security and Financial Crimes
doc_path: Rules of Licensing Finance Support Activities
Article 19: Requirements for Information Security and Financial Crimes
document_html:
1.The finance support company shall comply with the information security requirements issued by the bank.
 
2.The finance support company shall comply with the legal requirements set forth in the Anti-Money Laundering Law, the Law on Combating the Financing of Terrorism, their Implementing Regulations, and the relevant instructions and guidelines as specified by the bank, in a manner that is consistent with the nature and size of the company’s activity and risks it may be exposed to. The company shall also comply with the requirements and instructions issued by the bank on financial crimes and fraud.

title: Article 20: Saudization of Human Resources
doc_path: Rules of Licensing Finance Support Activities
document_html: At least 50% of all employees must be Saudi nationals when a finance support company starts operations. The percentage applies at the level of the company as a whole. The bank may increase or decrease the percentage as it deems appropriate.

title: Article 21: Code of Conduct
doc_path: Rules of Licensing Finance Support Activities
document_html: The finance support company shall develop a Code of Conduct and take all necessary actions to ensure compliance therewith in accordance with the relevant laws, regulations and instructions. This Code shall include clear principles, policies and controls for professional behavior with beneficiaries and the conflict of interest policy, to be approved by the highest authority in the company.

title: Article 22: Consumer Protection and Data Confidentiality
doc_path: Rules of Licensing Finance Support Activities
Article 22: Consumer Protection and Data Confidentiality
document_html:
1.The finance support company shall establish a function for handling complaints and set clear procedures for receiving, documenting, reviewing, and responding to complaints within the period set by the bank. The complaints shall be kept in records that include all necessary details of complaints and related actions taken.
 
2.The finance support company and its employees shall maintain the confidentiality of clients’ data and transactions and shall not disclose them to other parties or benefit from them even after leaving the job or revocation of license, except in accordance with the relevant laws and instructions.
 
3.The finance support company shall take all necessary measures to ensure confidentiality of clients’ information and transactions.

title: Article 23: The bank’s Supervision
doc_path: Rules of Licensing Finance Support Activities
document_html:
1.The finance support company shall:
 
 (a)provide the bank with any other data, information, or documents required in accordance with the forms, controls, and instructions and at the time set by the bank; 
 
 (b)provide the bank with all information and documents related to the company, its activities, partners, or staff immediately upon request;
 
 (c)develop and periodically update a policy on conflict of interest and confidentiality of information;
 
 (d)develop a business continuity plan and a recruitment plan for vacant positions; and
 
 (e)enable the bank’s specialized staff and auditors to access relevant facilities, documents and data, including digital data, upon request.
 
2.The finance support company and its staff shall not conceal or attempt to conceal any information or violations, or refrain from answering any inquiries made by the bank.
 
3.The bank may take necessary actions to ensure the compliance of finance support company with these Rules, relevant laws, regulations and instructions, such as making supervisory or inspection visits to the company headquarters, meeting its staff and reviewing its systems, procedures and records. The bank may appoint a third party, at the expense of the company, to carry out any of the procedures taken in accordance with the provisions stated in this Chapter.
 
4.If the company violates these Rules or the applicable laws and regulations, or has financial difficulties, the bank may take one or more of the following actions:
 
 (a)Issue business management instructions to the company’s senior management.
 
 (b)Ban or restrict all or some of the activities.
 
 (c)Prevent directors or senior management from exercising all or some of their duties.
 
 (d)Appoint supervisors to run the business of the company as determined by the bank.

title: Article 24: Compliance
doc_path: Rules of Licensing Finance Support Activities
document_html:
1.The finance support company shall establish internal controls and procedures to ensure compliance with these Rules and all relevant laws, regulations and instructions.
 
2.The finance support company shall keep sufficient records to confirm compliance with these Rules and other relevant laws, regulations and instructions, and take the necessary measures to prevent violations thereof.
 
3.The finance support company shall not disclose information to third parties without the approval of the bank.
 
4.The finance support company shall obtain the bank’s non-objection before acquiring assets other than those necessary to manage its business.
 
5.The finance support company shall obtain the bank’s non-objection before partial or full liquidation of the company or its activity.  
 
6.Non-compliance with these Rules shall be deemed a violation of the Finance Companies Control Law and its Implementing Regulation.

title: Article 25: Regulatory and Technical Instructions
doc_path: Rules of Licensing Finance Support Activities
document_html: The bank may issue regulatory and technical instructions for each finance support activity and the finance support company shall comply with these instructions.

title: Article 26: Exemption
doc_path: Rules of Licensing Finance Support Activities
document_html: Upon request, the bank may exempt the finance support company from the application of any of the provisions of these Rules as required by the condition of the sector.

title: Article 27: Enforcement
doc_path: Rules of Licensing Finance Support Activities
document_html: These Rules shall enter into force on the date of their approval.

title: 1. Definitions
doc_path: Section I: Definitions and General Provisions
document_html:
1.1The terms and phrases mentioned herein shall have the same meanings stated in the Rules of Licensing Finance Support Activities.
 
1.2The following terms and phrases, wherever used herein, shall have the corresponding meanings unless the context requires otherwise:
 
 1.2.1SAMA: The Saudi Central Bank.
 
 1.2.2Instructions: The Instructions for Practicing Aggregation Activity.
 
 1.2.3Activity: Aggregation activity.
 
 1.2.4Financier: Banks, finance companies, and entities licensed to engage in finance activities under the laws applicable in Saudi Arabia.
 
 1.2.5Consumer: A person to whom services are offered by the entity.
 
 1.2.6Entity: An entity licensed by SAMA to practice aggregation activity.
 
 1.2.7Platform: Any electronic means used to carry out the activity, including websites and applications.
 
 1.2.8Documented Channels: An approved, recorded and verifiable contact method that can be retrieved electronically, such as text messages and emails.

title: 2. General Provisions
doc_path: Section I: Definitions and General Provisions
document_html:
2.1These Instructions aim to set the minimum standards and procedures necessary for carrying out the activity.
 
2.2These Instructions shall apply to entities licensed by SAMA to engage in the activity.
 
2.3The activity shall not be carried out except after obtaining a license from SAMA in accordance with the Rules of Licensing Finance Support Activities and the relevant laws.
 
2.4These Instructions shall not prejudice the provisions contained in relevant laws and instructions, including, but not limited to, the following:
 
 2.4.1The Finance Companies Control Law issued by Royal Decree No. M/51 dated 13/08/1433H and its Implementing Regulations.
 
 2.4.2The Rules of Licensing Finance Support Activities issued by SAMA.
 
 2.4.3The Cyber Security Framework issued by SAMA.
 
 2.4.4The Business Continuity Management Framework issued by SAMA.
 
 2.4.5The Financial Consumer Protection Principles and Rules issued by SAMA.

title: 3. Technological Equipment
doc_path: Section II: Regulatory and Technical Instructions
document_html: The entity shall ensure that its technological equipment and related systems are sufficient for its operational needs and the nature of the activity and in line with the best practices and SAMA’s instructions issued in this regard. In addition, as a minimum, the entity shall maintain, develop and operate the platform to carry out the activity according to SAMA’s instructions and shall develop standard technical interfaces to communicate with financiers, exchange information, and receive and process finance offers and applications.

title: 4. Requirements for the Accuracy of Information Provided
doc_path: Section II: Regulatory and Technical Instructions
4. Requirements for the Accuracy of Information Provided
document_html:
4.1The entity shall, using reliable and independent sources, verify the identity of the consumer and ensure the validity of the information and documents provided online before sending them to the financier. Such procedure shall be documented in accordance with the instructions issued by SAMA.
 
4.2The entity shall establish the necessary internal procedures to ensure the validity and accuracy of finance offers before presenting them to the consumer.
 
4.3The entity shall create an electronic record for each consumer and comply with the Electronic Transactions Law and its Implementing Regulations. The entity shall also establish the necessary procedures and measures to ensure that the information provided is correct and up-to-date, including, at a minimum:
 
 4.3.1Sending an authentication code to verify the consumer’s phone number.
 
 4.3.2Developing the procedures necessary to ensure the provision of up-to-date information, such as the national address.

title: 5. Requirements for the Retention of Information Provided
doc_path: Section II: Regulatory and Technical Instructions
5. Requirements for the Retention of Information Provided
document_html:
Taking into account the laws and instructions related to data and information protection issued by the competent authorities, the entity shall, at a minimum: 
 
5.1Develop the necessary procedures and controls to maintain the confidentiality of all data and information obtained through the platform, and not disclose such data and information to any external party unless SAMA’s prior approval is obtained and in a manner consistent with the relevant regulations.
 
5.2Ensure the security, integrity and availability of the information provided through the platform, including, but not limited to, the information provided for the consumer and the information collected and stored by the entity or the other party it contracted with as a service provider. The entity shall particularly protect the consumer’s personal information from loss and unauthorized access, including use, modification and disclosure.
 
5.3Keep all consumer documents, records and files in an orderly, clear and safe manner and ensure that all files are complete and updated regularly, for a period of at least 10 years from the date of the end of the relationship with the consumer.

title: 6. Conflict of Interest
doc_path: Section II: Regulatory and Technical Instructions
document_html: The entity shall develop an appropriate written organizational policy that addresses potential conflicts of interest. Such policy must include adequate measures to be taken to avoid and address any conflict of interest to ensure fair treatment of all consumers and financiers.

title: 7. Disclosure
doc_path: Section II: Regulatory and Technical Instructions
document_html:
The entity shall: 
 
7.1Clarify and post on its platform all terms and conditions of the platform, security instructions, payment methods, information confidentiality, any other instructions related to the use of the platform, and all data that must be disclosed under the relevant laws and instructions.
 
7.2Disclose all fees and commissions charged for the entity’s services.
 
7.3Post on its platform the entity’s licensing information.

title: 8. Obligations of the Entity
doc_path: Section II: Regulatory and Technical Instructions
document_html:
8.1The entity shall strengthen the platform’s cybersecurity and promptly deal with any cases of breach. In case of a breach, the entity shall immediately notify SAMA.
 
8.2The entity shall ensure that the electronic linkage between the entity and the financier serves the provision of aggregation activity only and is not used for any other purposes, unless approved by SAMA.
 
8.3The entity shall have on its platform a feature that allows consumers to communicate directly with the entity to submit feedback and complaints. This feature must also allow for documentation and preservation of any communication occurring through it.
 
8.4The entity shall set appropriate approvals and acknowledgments and allow consumers to read and agree to them before using the platform, provided that such approvals and acknowledgments are shown as a Pop-Up Window.
 
8.5The entity shall inform, through the documented channels, the consumer of the reason if the finance application is not accepted or of the need to submit additional documents if required.
 
8.6The entity shall consider the needs and desires of consumers and provide them with information in a clear, transparent and not misleading manner.
 
8.7The entity shall provide visual and print messages and materials to raise awareness of and educate consumers about major risks, thus helping them make informed and effective decisions before obtaining finance from the financier.
 
8.8The entity shall not receive or deliver funds on behalf of the financier unless SAMA’s approval is obtained.
 
8.9The entity shall make a list of the financiers it deals with so that the consumer can choose from them.
 
8.10The entity shall not participate in any marketing campaigns for any financier and shall not prefer a financier to another.
 
8.11The entity shall obtain the consumer’s consent before examining their credit record held with one or more credit bureaus and before sharing the consumer’s credit information with the financier, in a manner consistent with the relevant laws and instructions.
 
8.12The entity shall offer the consumer the available financing options, provided that such options are consistent with the credit policies or standards communicated by the financier. If the financier’s credit policies or standards do not apply to the consumer, the entity shall explain the reasons to the consumer through the platform.
 
8.13In the event that finance is approved, the entity shall send a message to the consumer through the documented channels. The message must state the basic information of the finance product in a clear, accurate, understandable and not misleading manner, accompanied by the phone numbers of the complaint centers/customer service at the entity and the financier.
 
8.14The entity shall periodically update the information on services and products provided by the financier for the consumer. Such information must be clear, concise, understandable, accurate and not misleading and must include, at a minimum, the following:
 
 8.14.1Key conditions and features.
 
 8.14.2Clarification of the rights and responsibilities of each party.
 
 8.14.3Details of the prices and commissions charged by the financier.
 
 8.14.4Details of fines, risks and the mechanism for terminating the relationship, along with the consequences thereof.
 
 8.14.5Details about the alternative products and services offered by other financiers.

title: 9. Contract Signed Between Entity and Consumer
doc_path: Section III: Contract Requirements Between Parties
9. Contract Signed Between Entity and Consumer
document_html:
The entity shall draw up a contract between the entity and the consumer in accordance with the relevant legal requirements. Each party shall receive a copy of the contract that must clarify, at least, the following: 
 
9.1Contract parties.
 
9.2Contract scope.
 
9.3Contract term.
 
9.4Desired type of finance, its duration, specifications — if any — and requirements.
 
9.5Rights and obligations of the contract parties.
 
9.6Pricing and fee structure.
 
9.7Withdrawal procedures and conditions.
 
9.8Dispute resolution mechanism.
 
9.9Contract termination and expiration.
 
9.10Any other data or information required by SAMA.

title: 10. Contract Signed Between Entity and Financier
doc_path: Section III: Contract Requirements Between Parties
10. Contract Signed Between Entity and Financier
document_html:
The entity shall draw up a paper or electronic contract between the entity and the financier in accordance with the relevant legal requirements. Each party shall receive a copy of the contract that must clarify, at least, the following: 
 
10.1Contract parties.
 
10.2Financier’s licensing number and date.
 
10.3Contract scope.
 
10.4Contract term, provided that the contract term is consistent with the validity of relevant licenses of both parties.
 
10.5Rights and obligations of the contract parties.
 
10.6Pricing and fee structure.
 
10.7Mechanisms for exchanging data and information of finance offers and for updating them periodically.
 
10.8Withdrawal procedures and conditions.
 
10.9Service levels, performance requirements, and mechanisms of reporting and escalation.
 
10.10The financier’s obligation to notify the entity through the platform when the finance contract is issued.
 
10.11Dispute resolution mechanism.
 
10.12Information confidentiality, privacy and security.
 
10.13Commitment of the parties to fulfill the obligations stipulated in the relevant laws, regulations, rules, guidelines and instructions. The financier is not exempted from meeting its obligations.
 
10.14Prohibition of subcontracting.
 
10.15Consequences of contract renewal and renegotiation.
 
10.16Contract termination and expiration.
 
10.17Any other data or information required by SAMA.

title: Section IV: Concluding Provisions
document_html:
11.Non-compliance with these Instructions shall be deemed a violation of the Finance Companies Control Law.
 
12.SAMA may exempt the entity from applying any of the requirements contained in these Instructions.
 
13.These Instructions shall be published on the official website of SAMA and shall enter into force on the date of their approval.

title: Instructions for Publishing Sanctions
document_html:
Based on the powers vested in SAMA under the Finance Companies Control Law issued by Royal Decree No. M/51 dated 13/08/1433H and its implementing regulations, and in light of SAMA's supervisory and regulatory role over the financial institutions under its supervision, and with a view to applying the principles of justice and transparency to enhance confidence in the financial sector, and to enable data users and decision-makers, including shareholders, investors, creditors, and customers, to access information on penalties imposed by SAMA for violations of regulatory and supervisory instructions, the following is established:

  1. Paragraph (1) of Article (72) of the Implementing Regulations of the Finance Companies Control Law states: "Financing companies must provide SAMA with their annual financial statements, the auditor’s report, and the Board of Directors' report at least five working days before their publication date."
  2. Article (73) of the Implementing Regulations of the Finance Companies Control Law states: "Without prejudice to the requirements of other applicable regulations, the financing company shall establish its own website on the global information network (Internet) to publish... 4. The Board of Directors' report."

 

Therefore, the following must be adhered to:

First: Financing and refinancing companies must publish in their annual Board of Directors’ reports the violations for which executive decisions have been issued by SAMA under the section titled "SAMA Executive Decisions", This should include violations from the current fiscal year as well as from the previous fiscal year. title: Utilization of the Beneficial Owner Information Inquiry Service for Private Associations and Foundations
doc_path: Utilization of the Beneficial Owner Information Inquiry Service for Private Associations and Foundations
document_html:
Based on SAMA’s authorities to issue instructions related to the financial institutions under its supervision, pursuant to the provisions of Saudi Central Bank Law issued by Royal Decree No. (M/36) dated 11/04/1442H, and to the Anti-Money Laundering Law issued by Royal Decree No. (M/20) dated 05/02/1439H, and the Law on Combating the Financing of Terrorism issued by Royal Decree No. (M/21) dated 12/02/1439H, and with reference to the Implementing Regulation of the Anti-Money Laundering Law issued by the State of Security Presidency Decision No. (14525) dated 19/02/1439H, and the obligations therein imposed on financial institutions to apply due diligence measures, particularly with respect to identifying and verifying the identity of the beneficial owner.

We inform you that the National Center for Non-Profit Sector has launched a service enabling financial institutions to inquire about beneficial owner information from private associations and foundations via the Center’s website (https://es.ncnp.gov.sa/v5/beneficial-owner-disclosure).

Accordingly, SAMA emphasizes the necessity of utilizing the above-mentioned service to fulfill due diligence requirements towards the financial institutions' customers from private associations and foundations, by accessing the Center’s website. In the event that an undisclosed beneficial owner exists, or where discrepancies are identified in the beneficial owner information provided by the private associations or foundation, the financial institution must apply the due diligence measures in place, in line with the requirements for reporting suspicious transactions as stipulated in the relevant laws and regulations, and in a manner that does not contravene the provisions of the Personal Data Protection Law, its Implementing Regulation, and  SAMA's instructions . The Center should be notified via email at (AML-CFT.PL@NCNP.GOV.SA). Financial institutions may also, in case of any implementation challenges, contact the Financial Integrity General Department via email at (FIGD@SAMA.GOV.SA).

For your information and to action accordingly as of the date of its publication on SAMA’s website.

title: SAMAs' Notification Prior Conducting Investment Rounds
doc_path: SAMAs' Notification Prior Conducting Investment Rounds
document_html:
Based on the powers vested in the Saudi Central Bank pursuant to its Law issued by Royal Decree No. (M/36) dated 11/04/1442H, and other relevant laws, and stemming from its supervisory and regulatory role over the financial institutions under its supervision, and in pursuit of maintaining the soundness of the financial sector and supporting its growth.

We would like to inform you that non-bank financial institutions shall notify SAMA at least five (5) business days prior to conducting any investment rounds, provided that all information related to the investment round is submitted, including, but not limited to, the following:

  1. The timeline of the investment round.
     
  2. The objective of the investment round.
     
  3. The value of the investment round.
     
  4. The targeted category.
     
  5. A statement outlining the impact of the investment round on the ownership structure and financial position of the non-bank financial institution.
     
  6. The type and structure of the investment instrument (equity, convertible instruments, debt instruments, and others).
     
  7. Any other material or supporting documents.
     
  8. Any other documents requested by SAMA.
     

We further emphasize that the above shall not prejudice the obligations of non-bank financial institutions set out in the relevant laws and instructions, including obtaining SAMA’s prior non-objection where required.

For your information and action accordingly as of this date.

title: Emphasis on the Obligations of Finance Entities to Verify Cases of Economic Total Loss of Motor Vehicles Financially Leased to Individuals
doc_path: Emphasis on the Obligations of Finance Entities to Verify Cases of Economic Total Loss of Motor Vehicles Financially Leased to Individuals
document_html:
Based on the supervisory and regulatory role of the Saudi Central Bank, and pursuant to the powers granted thereto under the Saudi Central Bank Law issued by Royal Decree No. (M/36) dated 11/04/1442H, the Banking Control Law issued by Royal Decree No. (M/5) dated 22/02/1386H, the Finance Companies Control Law issued by Royal Decree No. (M/51) dated 13/08/1433H, the Finance Lease Law issued by Royal Decree No. (M/48) dated 13/08/1433H and its Implementing Regulation issued by the Governor’s Decision No. (1/MSHT) dated 14/04/1434H, and in reference to the Rules for Comprehensive Insurance of Motor Vehicles Financially Leased to Individuals issued by the Governor’s Decision No. (441/191) dated 02/12/1441H, and as part of SAMA’s continuous efforts to monitor and address the challenges faced by customers of financial institutions.

Accordingly, SAMA would like to emphasize to finance entities engaging in the motor vehicle finance lease activity the following:

  1. Verification of reliance on reports issued by valuation facilities licensed by the Saudi Authority for Accredited Valuers when determining the economic total loss of Motor Vehicles Financially Leased to Individuals damaged as a result of an Accident, for purposes of implementing the provisions of Article (22) of the Finance Lease Law, while taking into consideration the provisions set out in the Rules for Comprehensive Insurance of Motor Vehicles Financially Leased to Individuals and the Model Contract of the Financial Lease of Vehicles for Individuals.
     
  2. The finance entity shall, upon receiving notification of damage to the leased asset by the lessee, take all appropriate measures and exercise due diligence with all relevant parties to ensure the continued use and benefit of the Motor Vehicle Financially Leased before considering it an economic total loss.

For your information and action accordingly.

title: Emphasis on Compliance with the Regulation on the Responsibilities and Duties of the Safety, Prevention, and Fire Protection Officer
doc_path: Emphasis on Compliance with the Regulation on the Responsibilities and Duties of the Safety, Prevention, and Fire Protection Officer
document_html:
In reference to the Ministry of Interior’s circular, which refers to the updated Regulation on the Responsibilities and Duties of the Safety, Prevention, and Fire Protection Officer in Government and Private Sectors.

Accordingly, SAMA emphasizes that all Financial Institutions shall comply with the provisions of the aforementioned Regulation, including, in particular:

  1. Compliance with the appointment or assignment of a qualified Safety Officer in accordance with the prescribed conditions.
     
  2. Implementation of fire safety, prevention, and protection requirements and regulations, and ensuring their continuous readiness in accordance with applicable regulatory requirements.
     
  3. Conduct periodic inspection and maintenance of safety systems in accordance with applicable regulatory requirements.
     
  4. Preparation and updating of evacuation and emergency plans, and the conduct of periodic drills thereon.
     
  5. Documentation of safety works, inspections, and measures taken, and the maintenance of related records.
     

The Regulation can also be accessed through the website of the General Directorate of Civil Defense via the following link: (https://998.gov.sa).

title: Technical Integration with "Wathq" Service for Verifying the Identity of the Ultimate Beneficial Owner (UBO)
doc_path: Technical Integration with "Wathq" Service for Verifying the Identity of the Ultimate Beneficial Owner (UBO)
document_html:
With reference to the Saudi Central Bank Law, issued by Royal Decree No. (M/36) dated 11/04/1442H, and the powers it confers with respect to issuing regulations and directives related to financial institutions and their operations; and to the Anti-Money Laundering Law, issued by Royal Decree No. (M/20) dated 05/02/1439H; and the Law on Combating the Financing of Terrorism , issued by Royal Decree No. (M/21) dated 12/02/1439H; and with reference to the Implementing Regulations to the Anti-Money Laundering Law, issued pursuant to Presidency of State Security Decision No. (14525) dated 19/02/1439H; and the Ultimate Beneficial Owner (UBO) Rules issued by Minister of Commerce Decision No. (99) dated 05/06/1447H.

We inform you that the Ministry of Commerce has launched a service to inquire about the disclosed Ultimate Beneficial Owner (UBO) data of companies registered therein, available through the “Wathq” service, which enables access to updated and approved Ultimate Beneficial Owner data.

Accordingly, the Saudi Central Bank emphasizes on the importance of implementing technical integration with the “Wathq” service to verify the identity of the Ultimate Beneficial Owner, while ensuring full compliance with all relevant conditions, controls, and requirements. Financial institutions must notify the Ministry of Commerce via the platform in cases where an Ultimate Beneficial Owner (UBO) has not been disclosed by the company or where discrepancies in Ultimate Beneficial Owner information are identified, based on the outcomes of the due diligence measures conducted. This should be done without prejudice to the requirements for reporting suspicious transactions stipulated in the relevant laws and regulations, and in a manner that does not violate the provisions of the Personal Data Protection Law, its implementing regulations, and the instructions issued by the Saudi Central Bank.

Furthermore, the Saudi Central Bank should be notified of any implementation challenges via the email of the Financial Integrity General Department (FIGD@SAMA.GOV.SA).

This circular shall be effective as of the date of its publication on the Saudi Central Bank’s website.

title: Circular Re. Guidance on Assessing Business Risks Related to Money Laundering, Terrorist Financing, and Proliferation Financing
doc_path: Circular Re. Guidance on Assessing Business Risks Related to Money Laundering, Terrorist Financing, and Proliferation Financing
document_html:
With reference to the powers of SAMA to issue instructions related to financial institutions and their activities subject to its supervision and oversight, pursuant to the Saudi Central Bank Law issued by Royal Decree No (M/36) dated 11/4/1442H, and Anti-Money Laundering Law issued by Royal Decree No. (M/20) dated 5/2/1439H, and Law on Combating the Financing of Terrorism issued by Royal Decree No. (M/21) dated 12/2/1439H, and relevant Laws and Regulations.

Attached is the Guidance on Assessing Business Risks Related to Money Laundering, Terrorist Financing, and Proliferation Financing which aims to establish the minimum set of factors that a financial institution must take into consideration when conducting its business risk assessment. The Guide also sets out the key criteria and controls that must be observed in carrying out such an assessment the Guide also includes risk assessment methodologies commensurate with the nature of the financial institution’s activities, the scale of its operations, and its level of risk exposure, while emphasizing that it does not prescribe a single standardized risk assessment methodology. The factors, criteria, and controls set out in this Guide are not exhaustive and do not limit the obligations imposed on financial institutions under the relevant laws, regulations, and instructions relating to anti-money laundering, counter-terrorist financing, and counter-proliferation financing, nor does this Guide preclude a financial institution from adopting any additional measures necessary to fulfill its obligations in this regard.

For your information and action accordingly, as the date of publication of the Guide on SAMA's web.

title: Circular Re. Compliance with the Key Principles of Governance in Financial Institutions Subject to SAMA's Supervision
doc_path: Circular Re. Compliance with the Key Principles of Governance in Financial Institutions Subject to SAMA's Supervision
document_html:
Based on SAMA's supervisory and regulatory role, and based on the powers vested in it under the Saudi Central Bank Law issued by Royal Decree No. (M/36) dated 11/04/1442H, and other relevant regulations, and its keenness to enhance the effective management of financial institutions subject to its supervision.

We would like to inform you the obligation of all Finance Companies and Payment Services providers to comply with the Key Principles of Governance in Financial Institutions (The Principles) issued according to SAMA's Circular No. (42081293), dated 21/11/1442H. Such companies shall be required to comply with the provisions set forth therein, in accordance with the following procedures:

First: Conduct an assessment of the company’s current status with respect to governance procedures, and to develop a roadmap to achieve compliance with The Principles within the compliance period granted, as specified in Paragraph (Fourth).

Second: Obtain the approval of the Board of Directors / Managers for the prepared roadmap, and along with the necessary support for its implementation.

Third: Submit the assessment and the approved roadmap via email to (ComplianceFCC@SAMA.GOV.SA), no later than thirty (30) days from the date of issuance of this Circular. 

Fourth: Comply with The Principles no later than one (1) year from the date of issuance of this Circular, or upon the expiry of the term of the current Board of Directors / Managers, whichever occurs first. SAMA shall have the authority to extend the prescribed compliance period where justified.

For your information and action accordingly.

title: Decision on the Cancellation of SAMA's Licensing Requirement for Practicing the Finance Debt Collection Activity
doc_path: Decision on the Cancellation of SAMA's Licensing Requirement for Practicing the Finance Debt Collection Activity
document_html:
In line with SAMA’s supervisory and regulatory role, and pursuant to the powers vested in it under the Saudi Central Bank Law issued by Royal Decree No. (M/36) dated 11/04/1442H, and the Finance Companies Control Law issued by Royal Decree No. (M/51) dated 13/08/1433H; and with reference to the decision of His Excellency the Governor of the Saudi Central Bank approving the amendments to the Implementing Regulations of the Finance Companies Control Law, and the decision of His Excellency the Governor of the Saudi Central Bank approving the amendments to the Rules of Licensing Finance Support Activities.

We inform you that it has been decided to cancel the requirement for obtaining a license from SAMA to practice the finance debt collection activity. Furthermore, we emphasize the necessity for finance debt collection entities whether those previously licensed by SAMA or those that have obtained initial approval to comply with the relevant statutory provisions regarding the update of their activities in the commercial registers in accordance with this decision.

For your information and action accordingly.

title: Mechanism for Assigning Debt Collection Operations of Banks and Finance Companies to Finance Debt Collection Entities Licensed by SAMA
doc_path: Mechanism for Assigning Debt Collection Operations of Banks and Finance Companies to Finance Debt Collection Entities Licensed by SAMA
document_html:
In line with SAMA’s supervisory and regulatory role, and pursuant to the powers vested in it under its Law issued by Royal Decree No. (M/36) dated 11/04/1442H, the Finance Companies Control Law issued by Royal Decree No. (M/51) dated 13/08/1433H, and the Banking Control Law issued by Royal Decree No. (M/5) dated 22/02/1386H, which authorize SAMA to regulate the banking sector and the finance companies sector, and with reference to SAMA Circular No. (44055679) dated 08/07/1444H regarding the restriction of assigning debt collection operations of banks and finance companies to debt collection entities licensed by SAMA, effective as of 01/01/2024, and further to SAMA Circulars No. (45029088) dated 01/05/1445H, No. (45077226) dated 26/12/1445H, No. (46014147) dated 01/03/1446H, No. (106877869) dated 29/06/1446H, and No. (106893404) dated 25/09/1446H, regarding the assignment of debt collection operations for banks and finance companies to debt collection entities that have obtained SAMA's initial approval; and with reference to the decision of His Excellency the Governor approving the amendments to the Implementing Regulations of the Finance Companies Control Law, and the decision of His Excellency the Governor approving the amendments to the Rules of Licensing Finance Support Activities.

We inform you that it has been decided to supersede the application of the aforementioned circulars. Accordingly, the assignment of debt collection operations of banks and finance companies shall be made to entities that comply with the requirements and conditions stipulated in the applicable laws, regulations, and instructions, after obtaining a no-objection letter from SAMA for contracting with entities that conduct debt collection activities without the requirement that such entities be licensed by SAMA. This shall be without prejudice to the provisions of the relevant laws, rules, and instructions, including those related to outsourcing, debt collection, and customer protection.

For your information and action accordingly.

title: Not to Request Promissory Notes from Individual Consumers when Offering a Credit Card Financing Products
doc_path: Not to Request Promissory Notes from Individual Consumers when Offering a Credit Card Financing Products
document_html:
In line with the supervisory and regulatory role of SAMA, and pursuant to the powers vested in it under the Saudi Central Bank Law issued by Royal Decree No. (M/36) dated 11/4/1442H, the Banking Control Law issued by Royal Decree No. (M/5) dated 22/2/1386H, and the Finance Companies Control Law issued by Royal Decree No. (M/51) dated 13/8/1433H; and referring to the Instructions for creditors on dealing with Promissory Notes issued under Circular No. (43076917) dated 4/9/1443H; and in view of the recent observation of the widespread practice of obtaining promissory notes from individual consumers when offering credit card financing products.

Accordingly, and without prejudice to the obligations and responsibilities of finance entities set out in the relevant laws and regulations, including the Responsible Lending Principles to Individuals consumers; Finance entities must cease requesting promissory notes or any other negotiable instruments from individual consumers when offering credit card financing products. Finance entities are also required to update their internal policies, procedures, and controls to ensure compliance with this requirement.

For your information and action accordingly as of 1 February 2026. Finance entities must provide SAMA (Consumer Protection Supervision Department) within (30) days from the date of this circular with a remediation plan to rectify existing practices. At a minimum, the plan must include the return or cancellation of promissory notes or negotiable instruments previously obtained from individual consumers that are not compliant with this circular. The implementation of the plan must not exceed one (6) month from the date of this circular.

title: Circular Re. the Rules for the Implementation of Targeted Financial sanctions
doc_path: Circular Re. the Rules for the Implementation of Targeted Financial sanctions
document_html:
Referring to SAMA Circular No. (391000014326) dated 06/02/1439H, supplementary to Circular No. (381000077863) dated 22/07/1438H regarding the Mechanisms for the Implementation of Security Council Resolutions relating to Combating Terrorism and its Financings; and referring to SAMA Circular No. (391000054107) dated 12/05/1439H regarding the Mechanism for Implementation of Security Council resolutions related to Prevention of Proliferation of weapons of Mass Destruction and their Financing; and SAMA Circular No. (130885/486) dated 04/09/1440H, supplementary to Circular No. (391000077627) dated 09/07/1439 H regarding the update of the Guide to Enforcing Security Council Resolutions Concerning the Prevention of WMD Proliferation and Their Financing; and referring to the telegram from the Presidency of State Security No. (103215) dated 08/05/1447H regarding the third update of the mechanisms for implementing Security Council resolutions related to combating terrorism and its financing issued by the Permanent Counter Terrorism Committee; and referring to Royal Order No. (10130) dated 01/03/1439H approving the mechanism for implementing Security Council resolutions issued under Chapter Seven of the United Nations Charter related to the prevention of the proliferation of weapons of mass destruction and their financing.

Enclosed herewith are the Rules for the Implementation of Targeted Financial Sanctions, which aim to establish the minimum obligations related to the Implementation of Targeted Financial Sanctions concerning combating terrorism and its financing and the prevention of the proliferation of weapons of mass destruction and their financing. The provisions of the Rules shall be mandatorily applied to all financial institutions subject to the supervision and oversight of SAMA. These Rules supersede the aforementioned circulars. The financial institution must present the Rules to its Board of Directors—or the equivalent governing body in the case of financial institutions not incorporated as joint-stock companies—and define the responsibilities of the Board, senior management, and relevant administrative units in relation to these Rules. The financial institutions may contact SAMA to provide immediate reporting of any matches or to raise inquiries related to these Rules through the following email: (TFS-FIGD@SAMA.GOV.SA ).

For your information and action accordingly effective from the date of its publication on SAMA’s website.

title: Sharing Residential Real Estate Finance Data with the Saudi Credit Bureau (SIMAH)
doc_path: Sharing Residential Real Estate Finance Data with the Saudi Credit Bureau (SIMAH)
document_html:
Based on the Saudi Central Bank Law issued by Royal Decree No. (M/36) dated 11/4/1442 H, the Credit Information Law issued by Royal Decree No. (M/37) dated 5/7/1429 H, the Banking Control Law issued by Royal Decree No. (M/5) dated 22/2/1386 H, and the Finance Companies Control Law issued by Royal Decree No. (M/51) dated 13/8/1433 H. And in reference to SAMA'S efforts to support the integration of the financial sector system, the informational linkage between finance entities, and the enhancement of transparency and credit assessment monitoring by providing tools that contribute to mitigating credit risks associated with financial transactions across any economic activity.  

Accordingly, SAMA emphasizes the obligation of all finance entities to share individual data related to residential real estate finance with the Saudi Credit Bureau (SIMAH), in accordance with the guidelines and templates that will be shared in this regard, while emphasizing the importance of adherence to the regulations and instructions issued by SAMA and other relevant regulatory entities, as well as the provisions of the Personal Data Protection Law.

For your information and action accordingly effective from its date.

title: Providing Postal Service Providers with the National Address
doc_path: Providing Postal Service Providers with the National Address
document_html:
In reference to the powers of SAMA to issue instructions related to the Financial Institutions under its supervision, and pursuant to the provisions of the Saudi Central Bank Law issued under Royal Decree No. (M/36) dated 11/04/1442H, and the relevant laws; and in reference to Circular No. (371000068810) dated 19/06/1437H, as a follow-up to SAMA's Circular No. (351000101674) dated 06/08/1435H regarding the approval of arrangements for implementing the provisions related to residence and work addresses; SAMA emphasizes on the necessity of linking the provision of various customer services to the approved address data (National Address) registered with the Saudi Postal and Logistics Services Company (SPL); and with reference to the Transport General Authority Decision No. (196/46/1) dated 08/10/1446H, which obliges postal service providers not to accept mail shipments that are not labeled with the National Address starting from 01/01/2026G.

title: Launch of the First Phase of the Complaint Management System
doc_path: Launch of the First Phase of the Complaint Management System
document_html:
Based on the powers vested in the Saudi Central Bank under its law issued by Royal Decree No. (M/36) dated 11/4/1442 H, and other relevant regulations, and in continuation of SAMA’s supervisory and regulatory role in establishing instructions and procedures aimed at protecting customers of financial institutions under its supervision, and in its ongoing efforts to promote trust in the financial sector and improve the quality of services provided by financial institutions to positively contribute to customer satisfaction.

We would like to inform you that SAMA has developed a Complaints Management System for customers of financial institutions supervised and regulated by SAMA “Complaints Management System”, and has launched the first phase of this system. The aim is to enhance transparency, improve the speed and effectiveness of financial institutions' responses to customer complaints*, process them efficiently, ensure compliance with service provision timelines and complaint handling periods, and improve the experience of customers in these financial institutions according to the best performance standards.

Accordingly, and in order to achieve the stated goals, financial institutions must adhere to the following:

First/ Complaints must be fully handled through the Complaints Management System within the following time frames:

NoComplaint Handling Time Frames
1Handling the customer complaint at (Level One) within a maximum of (5) business days from the date of its submission.
 
2Handling the customer complaint at (Level Two) - if escalated by the customer - within a maximum of (3) business days from the date the complaint is escalated.
 
3Responding to requests from SAMA regarding the complaint that has been accepted for escalation in objection to the financial institution's response, accurately and completely within a maximum of (2) business days from the date of the request.
 

 

Second/ Achieving Performance Indicators on a Quarterly Basis as Follows:

Classification

Indicator

Description of the Indicator

Percentage

Key Performance Indicators for Handling Complaints 

Quality of Customer Complaint Handling

Complaints handled by the financial institution at (Level One) and directly accepted by customers, in addition to complaints falling under customer acceptance behavior and deemed closed automatically, after excluding the percentage of escalated complaints.

Not less than 75%

Efficiency of Handling Complaints Escalated to Level Two

Complaints handled by the financial institution at (Level Two) and directly accepted by customers, in addition to complaints falling under customer acceptance behavior and deemed closed automatically, after excluding the percentage of escalated complaints.

Not less than 80%

 Complaints Escalated to SAMA

Complaints that have been accepted for escalation by SAMA.

Not more than 15%

Indicators for Complaint Handling Time Frames

 Compliance with Specified Time Frames for (Level One) Complaint Handling

Complaints handled within (5) working days at (Level One).

Not less than 95%

 Compliance with Specified Time Frames for (Level Two) Complaint Handling

Complaints handled within (3) working days at (Level Two).

Not less than 95%

 Compliance with the Specified Time Frames for Responding to SAMA

Complaints for which responses were provided to SAMA within two (2) business days.

Not less than 95%

Indicators for Compliant Handling Effectiveness

 Quality of Responses

Complaints closed after a single correspondence between SAMA and the financial institution.

Not less than 97%

Customer Recurrence

The number of customers who have more than one complaint compared to the total number of customers who submitted complaints through the Complaint Management System.

Not more than 25%

 Use of Missing Documents

Complaints in which missing documents were requested from customers, compared to the total number of complaints.

Not more than 15%

 

Third/ Providing the necessary support (technical, technological, and human resources) to the administrative units responsible for customer care, and granting them all the required authorities to perform their tasks with high proficiency and professionalism. This aims to effectively handle customer complaints within the specified time frames and regulations.

Fourth/ Reviewing and developing internal policies and procedures in line with this circular, updating service level agreements with the relevant departments accordingly, and improving the internal escalation mechanism through technological systems that ensure rapid escalation to the highest executive position, in order to achieve prompt and effective handling of complaints.

For your information and action accordingly as of its date. SAMA will monitor the extent of financial institutions’ compliance with the handling time frames and performance indicators, and will take regulatory measures against non-compliant financial institutions starting from the fourth quarter of 2025. It is worth noting that this circular supersedes any conflicting previous instructions issued by SAMA.

* Please refer to circular No. (371000101671), dated 17/9/1437H, regarding the "Complaint" Definition.

title: Circular Re. Rules of Issuance and Operation of Credit Cards
doc_path: Circular Re. Rules of Issuance and Operation of Credit Cards
document_html:

title: Circular Re. Counter-Fraud Fundamental Requirements
document_html:
Based on the Saudi Central Bank Law issued in Royal Decree No. (M/36) dated 11/04/1442H, and in accordance with the powers vested in it by the relevant regulations, and in line with its supervisory and regulatory role, and its commitment to enhancing practices within the financial sector to mitigate the risks of fraud and emerging fraudulent methods.

We would like to inform you of the adoption of the Counter-Fraud Fundamental Requirements Framework, which aims to strengthen counter-fraud practices through the implementation of a set of control measures designed to proactively enhance the maturity of institutions in addressing risks, patterns, and evolving methods of fraud.

Accordingly, finance companies and payment services providers are required to comply with the contents of the Framework in accordance with the following procedures:

First: The Member Organization must conduct a comprehensive and accurate assessment of its current counter-fraud measures in comparison with the Counter-Fraud Fundamental Requirements Framework (Gap Assessment), in order to identify areas of weakness and evaluate the Member Organization’s current maturity level.

Second: The Member Organization must develop a Roadmap to ensure full compliance with all requirements outlined in the Framework, following a thorough assessment of the current state within the institution’s environment. The prepared Roadmap must be approved by the institution’s Board of Directors and must include the necessary support for its implementation, taking into consideration the provisions of paragraph (Fifth).

Third: The Member Organization must submit the comprehensive assessment and the approved Roadmap to SAMA no later than the end of July 2025G.

Fourth: The Member Organization is required to provide SAMA with quarterly reports on the status of compliance with the framework, starting from the end of the third quarter of 2025G and continuing until full compliance with the requirements is achieved.

Fifth: The Member Organization must achieve full compliance with the Counter-Fraud Fundamental Requirements Framework no later than April 13, 2026G.

Sixth: The Member Organization must prepare a detailed report—issued by the Internal Audit Department (with the option to engage external experts)—outlining the status of compliance with the Counter-Fraud Fundamental Requirements Framework by the end of the second quarter of 2026G.

Seventh: The required submissions outlined above must be sent to SAMA via email at: (DAFS@SAMA.GOV.SA).

Eighth: The Counter-Fraud Fundamental Requirements Framework shall replace the Anti-Fraud Rules for Finance Companies, issued under Saudi Central Bank Circular No. (381000103246) dated 19/10/1438H, effective as of April 13, 2026G.

Please note that SAMA will conduct periodic inspection visits to verify the accuracy of the assessments and the level of compliance with the Counter-Fraud Fundamental Requirements Framework.

title: Implementation of the Provisions of the Commercial Register Law and the Law of Tradenames
doc_path: Implementation of the Provisions of the Commercial Register Law and the Law of Tradenames
document_html:
With reference to Royal Decree No. (M/83) dated 19/3/1446H, approving the Commercial Register Law and the Law of Tradenames, and with reference to Clause (Third) of the aforementioned Royal Decree, which grants those registered in the Commercial Register a period of five years from the effective date of the Commercial Register Law to correct the status of their subsidiary commercial registers, and the provisions of article (15) of the Commercial Register Law regarding the suspension of registration in the Commercial Register, and the article (29) stipulating that this Law shall replace the previous Commercial Register Law issued by Royal Decree No. (M/1) dated 21/2/1416H, and that it shall enter into force one hundred and eighty (180) days following its publication in the Official Gazette, and based on the powers granted to SAMA under its Law issued by Royal Decree No. (M/36) dated 11/4/1442H, and the relevant laws and regulations.

SAMA emphasizes the importance of implementing the provisions of the Commercial Register Law and the Law of Tradenames issued by Royal Decree No. (M/83) dated 19/3/1446H, including the following:

  1. Correct the status of the commercial registration of banks within the specified grace period and in accordance with the mechanisms approved by the Ministry of Commerce, and take all necessary measures to avoid any potential negative consequences in the future.
     
  2. Urge customers to correct the status of their commercial registrations within the specified grace period and in accordance with the mechanisms approved by the Ministry of Commerce, and take all necessary measures to avoid any potential negative consequences in the future.
     
  3. Verify the continued validity of customers' registration in the Commercial Register, and ensure that appropriate measures are taken in the event of suspension of the registration in accordance with the provisions of Article (15) of the Commercial Register Law. The suspension of a commercial registration shall be treated in the same manner as the expiration of the commercial register.
     
  4. Taking into account the provisions of paragraph (a) of Article (12) of the Rules Regulating Money Changing Business, which stipulate that any party wishing to engage in more than one activity (other than the money changing business) must establish a company instead of operating as a sole proprietorship, in accordance with the relevant laws and instructions, or take the necessary steps to liquidate the other activities conducted under the sole proprietorship that are not related to money changing business.

title: Providing SAMA with Audited Annual Financial Statements, the Quarterly Financial Statements, and the Prudential Data
doc_path: Providing SAMA with Audited Annual Financial Statements, the Quarterly Financial Statements, and the Prudential Data
document_html:
Based on the powers granted to SAMA under the relevant laws and Instructions, we would like to inform you that licensed aggregation companies are required to comply with the following:

First: Provide SAMA with the quarterly financial statements and the auditor’s report within (20) twenty business days from the end of each of the months of March, June, and September of each Gregorian year.

Second: Provide SAMA with the audited annual financial statements and the auditor’s report within (45) forty-five business days from the end of the Gregorian year.

Third: Provide SAMA with the annual and quarterly prudential data in accordance with the attached approved models, ensuring the accuracy of all submitted information.
The quarterly prudential data models must be submitted within (25) twenty-five business days from the end of each of the months of March, June, September, and December, while the annual prudential data models must be submitted within (60) sixty business days from the end of the Gregorian year to SAMA.

Fourth: The prudential data models, once completed as required, must be submitted electronically in Excel format within the timeframes specified in Clause (Third) above. A scanned electronic copy of the Certification Statement must also be provided after being signed by the Chief Accountant, Chief Financial Officer (CFO), and the Chief Executive Officer (CEO) or Managing Director, as applicable.

Fifth: The annual prudential data models must be reviewed by the company's External Auditor before being submitted to SAMA. A signed copy of the audit certificate issued by the External Auditor must be attached to the submitted models.

For your information and compliance, effective starting from the second quarter of 2025.
